newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's ERB approves 4.82 centavos power rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Manila's ERB approves 4.82 centavos power rate cut.

text.p: The Philippine's Energy Regulatory Board (ERB) said on Friday it has approved a 4.82 centavo per kilowatt-hour (kwh) average reduction in power rates for the main northern island of Luzon.
"We approved the whole thing effective today," ERB chairman Bayani Faylona told Reuters adding that the board will announce its approval at a news briefing at noon.
Faylona said the state-run National Power Corp (Napocor) had applied for the reduction early this year to pass on savings as a result of improvements in power plant efficiency.

Napocor tariff manager Edgardo Orencia said the reduction in basic rates will be the first time after five years. Basic rates cover the cost of electricity generated without reflecting the forex movements and monthly fuel cost fluctuations.
Napocor charges a basic rate of 1.84 pesos per kwh in Luzon which accounts for 76 percent of the sales of the country's biggest power generation company.
Faylona said the Manila Electric Co (Meralco), Napocor's largest customer, will be required to pass on the reduction to customers.
